examples.japanese: {暴政|ぼうせい}に{苦|くる}しむ{民衆|みんしゅう}。
{国民|こくみん}は{暴政|ぼうせい}に{対|たい}して{立|た}ち{上|あ}がった。
examples.english: The citizens rose up against the tyrannical rule.

examples.japanese: {歴史|れきし}の{教科書|きょうかしょ}には、{暴政|ぼうせい}を{敷|し}いた{王|おう}の{話|はなし}が{数多|かずおお}く{載|の}っている。
examples.english: History textbooks contain many stories of kings who imposed tyrannical rule.

notes:
Describes cruel and oppressive governance by a ruler or government. Frequently encountered in historical and political contexts.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {暴政|ぼうせい}を{敷|し}く: to impose tyranny
- {暴政|ぼうせい}に{苦|くる}しむ: to suffer under tyranny
- {暴政|ぼうせい}に{立|た}ち{向|む}かう: to stand up against tyranny
- {暴政|ぼうせい}を{倒|たお}す: to overthrow a tyranny

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {独裁|どくさい}: dictatorship — rule by a single person, not necessarily cruel
- {圧政|あっせい}: oppression — similar in meaning but emphasizes the weight of authoritarian control
- {苛政|かせい}: harsh government — emphasizes cruelty and harshness in governance; more literary
